Coupon SERP Landscape Analysis¶

This report analyzes the SERP landscape for coupon-intent queries across five markets: DE, ES, FR, IT, and NL. These searches reflect strong transactional intent, where users actively look for promo codes, discounts, and special offers.

The goal of this analysis is to understand how coupon-intent SERPs differ across markets, identify the domains and SERP features that dominate these searches, and assess the organic and AI Overview visibility of Cybernews (cybernews.com). The analysis also looks for areas where stronger coupon coverage or product-specific content could create additional visibility opportunities.

Datasets¶

The analysis is based on two complementary datasets:

  • Quantitative dataset – keyword-level SERP feature presence (organic, AI Overviews, Top Stories, and other modules)
  • Qualitative dataset – individual SERP items including domains, rankings, citations, and positions

The number of tracked queries differs by locale, and both absolute counts and normalized metrics are used where appropriate to ensure fair cross-market comparisons.

Report Structure¶

The report follows a structured approach:

  1. Overall SERP feature distribution across all markets
  2. Locale deep dives, including:
    • dominant organic domains (by appearances and #1 rankings)
    • AI Overview source dominance
    • Cybernews organic and AIO visibility and ranking distributions
    • keyword-level insights and associated products
  3. Product-specific analyses for key brands such as NordVPN and Proton VPN, evaluating competitive landscapes and Cybernews’ performance within these segments

Note:
Full domain-level competitor lists for AI Overviews, and organic results (by market) are provided as CSV files in the repository for reference.

SERP Feature Distribution¶

To establish the overall search landscape, I begin by examining SERP feature prevalence across all five markets.

Next, I break down SERP feature prevalence at the individual market level to highlight differences in how coupon results pages are structured across locales.

This view helps identify where features like AI Overviews, Top Stories, or other SERP elements are more prominent and where organic visibility may face stronger competition.

Across the analyzed markets, organic results remain consistently present, while Related Searches and Related Questions are also prominent features of coupon SERPs. Beyond these core elements, SERP composition varies more noticeably by locale, particularly for AI Overviews, video results, and the occasional Top Stories module.

Because AI Overviews and Top Stories introduce distinct visibility and competitive surfaces beyond traditional organic rankings, I examine both features in more detail below.

Top Stories Prevalence¶

While Top Stories are generally uncommon for coupon and discount-focused queries, a small number of keywords still trigger them across certain markets.

To better understand where these appear and whether they represent meaningful competitive surfaces, I briefly examine their prevalence by locale and review the specific queries that activated this feature.

Top Stories appear only sporadically within the coupon dataset and are primarily concentrated in the FR locale for brand-specific queries such as Hostinger and Bitdefender. These results are not driven by timely news or regulatory events.

Instead, the module surfaces informational and reputation-focused content:

Hostinger results included:

  • Wikipedia company overview pages (brand information)
  • iGraal cashback/review listings
  • Business Bacon and Website Planet affiliate-style reviews and comparisons

Bitdefender results included:

  • Wikipedia brand page
  • Official Bitdefender product pages
  • Trustpilot reputation listings
  • Journal du Geek editorial product tests

These pages focus on brand information, reviews, product evaluation, and credibility rather than discounts themselves. In this dataset, Top Stories therefore appear to function more as a brand-context and trust surface than as direct competition for coupon-focused pages.

Note: A single ES instance was triggered by a seasonal Black Friday keyword and reflects temporary shopping coverage rather than typical coupon SERP behavior. I treat this instance as an outlier.

AI Overview (AIO) Prevalence¶

The chart below shows the percentage of keywords that trigger an AI Overview in each locale.

AIO prevalence is high across most analyzed markets, particularly in IT (81%) and NL (75%), where AI Overviews appear for the majority of coupon queries.

This indicates that AI Overview visibility forms a meaningful part of the search landscape for coupon-intent queries in these markets, making source citations relevant alongside traditional organic rankings.

Note: FR shows 0% prevalence; however, this reflects an API limitation where AI Overview data is not currently returned for this locale rather than true absence on Google.

The following sections examine market-level differences in SERP structure, dominant domains, and Cybernews' organic and AI Overview visibility.

Top Domains in Germany (DE)¶

To establish the competitive landscape in Germany, I first examine the domains with the highest overall SERP appearance frequency across the coupon keyword set. Domain dominance is defined as the number of times a domain appears across visibility-driving SERP elements, including organic results, Top Stories, and AI Overview sources.

The German coupon SERP landscape is led primarily by deal aggregators and voucher platforms, although brand-owned domains also hold substantial visibility.

Several clear domain groups emerge:

  • Deal / coupon aggregators: mydealz.de, sparwelt.de, gutscheinsammler.de, rabattcode.de, coupons.de, gutegutscheine.de, einfach-sparsam.de
    These platforms account for a large share of repeated SERP appearances, highlighting the strong visibility of dedicated deal and voucher sites for coupon-intent searches.

  • Brand-owned domains: nordvpn.com, surfshark.com, protonvpn.com, proton.me
    Official vendors rank consistently, indicating that Google strongly favors first-party offers for transactional queries.

  • Community / UGC platforms: reddit.com, youtube.com
    User discussions, reviews, and promo code videos frequently surface, suggesting informational + trust signals play a role alongside pure coupon pages.

  • Student/discount programs: iamstudent.de, studentbeans.com
    Student-focused discount portals form a distinct niche and repeatedly appear for deal-related searches.

  • Editorial publishers: businessinsider.de
    Indicates that “best deals” or “discount roundups” from media sites occasionally compete with dedicated coupon platforms.

  • translate.google.com (44 appearances)
    These are not actual competitors. translate.google.com appears frequently in Related Questions and occasionally within AI Overviews. These are automatically translated proxy links generated by Google rather than true competing domains.

Next, I examine the organic ranking distribution for Cybernews (cybernews.com/de) to understand where its visibility is concentrated across the first page of results.

Cybernews maintains visibility across the full first page, but relatively few appearances reach the very top organic position. Germany — Key Findings¶

Overall, Germany shows a clear difference between traditional organic and AI-driven visibility. The highest organic position is heavily concentrated around a small number of competitors, particularly mydealz.de, while Cybernews has a comparatively stronger presence within AI Overviews than at the very top of the organic results.

Cybernews' strongest organic rankings are concentrated around Proton and 1Password-related queries, whereas its top AIO citations are distributed across a broader range of products. This suggests that, within the German coupon dataset, AI Overviews currently provide a particularly strong visibility surface for Cybernews alongside its established organic presence.

Remaining markets – summary approach¶

The remaining markets — ES, IT, NL, and FR — are analyzed in a condensed format, focusing on the main competitive patterns and Cybernews' organic and AI Overview visibility.

Complete domain-level competitor lists for organic results and AI Overview sources are included as separate CSV files in the repository for detailed reference.

Potential Opportunity — France¶

Cybernews' strongest French rankings are concentrated around NordVPN queries with more specific promotional intent, including YouTube and sponsor-code searches, while broader coupon SERPs are heavily occupied by established deal platforms.

A potential opportunity is therefore to expand around these more specific product + promotion-type query patterns rather than competing primarily for broad generic coupon terms (e.g. creating pages for topics like "Best NordVPN Youtuber discount codes"). Similar content could be tested for other products where Cybernews already has topical visibility, using variants such as influencer codes, sponsor codes, YouTube promotions, or other product-specific discount searches.

Because AI Overview data is unavailable for France, this opportunity is based on organic search performance only.

Cross-market comparison of organic visibility¶

The visualization below compares how Cybernews ranks organically across the five analyzed markets.
Each line represents the number of appearances at a given organic position (1–10).

It must be noted that the amount of content each locale owns has an influence on the number of appearances in SERP.

Germany shows the broadest organic footprint in the dataset, with Cybernews appearing consistently across the first page and a substantial share of rankings already sitting within positions where further upward movement is realistic.

The Netherlands also shows meaningful first-page coverage, although more of this visibility is concentrated outside the highest-ranking positions. Spain follows a similar pattern on a smaller scale, while France and Italy have much smaller organic footprints.

Note on comparability (absolute vs normalized):
The chart above shows absolute appearance counts. Because the number of keywords (and overall content footprint) differs by locale, markets with larger query sets can naturally produce higher counts.
To enable a more comparable view across locales, the following chart shows normalized appearances per 100 keywords.

Cross-Market Organic Opportunity¶

The normalized view helps separate ranking performance from differences in keyword-set size and provides a clearer picture of where Cybernews already has competitive first-page visibility.

Across the markets, the most immediate opportunity lies in queries where Cybernews already ranks on the first page but has not yet reached the highest positions. These rankings already demonstrate relevance, making them strong candidates for further optimization — particularly where the associated products are commercially important.

Germany, the Netherlands, and Spain show the clearest examples of this pattern, with a meaningful share of Cybernews rankings sitting below the top positions. In these cases, the priority would be to assess existing pages for potential improvements such as stronger alignment with coupon intent, content refreshes, internal linking, or gaps relative to higher-ranking competitors.

Markets with a smaller visibility footprint require a different interpretation. Some gaps may reflect weaker rankings for existing content, while others may simply indicate that relevant coupon coverage does not yet exist. Distinguishing between ranking gaps and content gaps therefore helps determine whether the better opportunity is to optimize an existing page or expand coverage into new query areas.

Across all five locales, NordVPN coupon queries show a highly consistent SERP structure dominated by three recurring domain types:

1) First-party ownership (brand control)

  • nordvpn.com ranks #1 in nearly every market
  • support.nordvpn.com frequently appears within the top 10

2) Local deal aggregators (structural dominance) Each market is led by 1–2 dominant native coupon platforms:

  • DE → mydealz.de, sparwelt.de
  • ES → chollometro.com, cupones.es
  • FR → dealabs.com, igraal.com
  • IT → trovaprezzi.it
  • NL → pepper.com, acties.nl

3) Community / trust sources

  • reddit.com
  • student discount portals (StudentBeans, UNiDAYS)
  • occasional editorial publishers

This suggests Google also values social proof and user validation alongside pure coupon listings.

Note on trust sources:
Rather than competing exclusively with large-scale aggregator platforms — which benefit from massive backlink profiles and thousands of pages — you might find stronger opportunities in “trust source” content. Examples include tested coupon guides, personal experience write-ups, verified working codes, and FAQ-style savings explainers. This approach aligns more closely with Cybernews’ editorial strengths and may provide a more scalable path to visibility compared to directly replicating aggregator models.

Cybernews' NordVPN visibility is generally stronger within AI Overviews than at the top of the organic results.

Germany shows the clearest example, with Cybernews frequently appearing toward the upper part of the AIO citation order across a broad set of NordVPN coupon variants. The Netherlands follows a similar pattern: organic NordVPN rankings are relatively weak, while AIO citations reach substantially stronger positions.

Spain also shows evidence of this difference, with Cybernews reaching a high AIO citation position despite limited organic NordVPN visibility. Italy has a smaller overall footprint, with Cybernews appearing in both organic and AIO results but without the same degree of top-position AIO visibility seen in Germany or the Netherlands.

NordVPN Visibility Takeaway¶

The NordVPN analysis shows that Cybernews visibility is distributed differently across traditional organic results and AI Overviews.

In several cases, Cybernews appears prominently as an AIO source while the same query shows weaker or no separate Cybernews organic placement. These cases should not automatically be interpreted as organic ranking gaps, since part of the available visibility is already being captured through the AI Overview surface.

The more useful comparison is therefore total SERP visibility across both surfaces: identifying queries where Cybernews is visible organically, within AIOs, across both, or not represented at all.

Queries with no Cybernews presence across either surface represent clearer visibility gaps, while queries already covered through AIO may require a different prioritization than their organic position alone would suggest.

For queries where Cybernews already captures one of these surfaces, the next step would be to evaluate which type of visibility is more commercially valuable. If an AIO citation drives stronger engagement or conversions than a lower organic ranking, preserving or strengthening AIO visibility may be the better priority; if traditional organic placements generate greater value, optimization efforts could instead focus on improving the organic position.

Conclusions & Opportunities¶

The analysis shows that coupon-intent SERPs differ substantially by market. Dedicated coupon and deal platforms are recurring organic competitors, but the strength of individual domains, Cybernews' existing visibility, and the role of AI Overviews vary enough that the same optimization strategy would not apply equally across all five locales.

Market-Level Opportunities¶

Germany offers the largest pool of existing rankings to work with.
Cybernews has the broadest first-page organic visibility in the dataset, although much of it remains below the highest positions. Germany therefore provides a strong set of existing rankings that can be evaluated for further improvement, particularly for commercially important products. At the same time, strong AIO visibility means organic rankings should not be assessed in isolation.

The Netherlands shows a similar organic-vs-AIO split.
Cybernews has meaningful first-page coverage, but its strongest visibility is more apparent within AI Overviews than at the top of the organic results. For relevant queries, the value of improving an organic position should therefore be assessed against the visibility already captured through AIO.

Spain is highly competitive organically, but AIO provides an additional route to visibility.
The highest organic positions are strongly occupied by established coupon domains, while Cybernews achieves comparatively stronger placements within AIOs. This makes AIO an important part of the visibility opportunity in Spain rather than treating traditional organic rankings as the only target.

Italy currently represents a narrow, product-specific footprint.
Cybernews' coupon visibility is relatively small and heavily concentrated around NordVPN. Before prioritizing optimization, the more useful next step is to determine whether commercially relevant product areas already have content that underperforms or whether meaningful coupon coverage is simply missing.

France reveals a distinct long-tail promotional opportunity.
Cybernews' strongest French NordVPN rankings include more specific promotional searches around YouTube, sponsor, and influencer codes. Similar product + promotion-type query patterns could be explored for other commercially relevant products, particularly where broader coupon terms are heavily occupied by established deal platforms.

Overall, the findings support a market- and product-specific strategy: optimize existing visibility where Cybernews already has traction, expand into genuine content gaps where coverage is missing, and evaluate organic and AIO opportunities according to their commercial value.

Further Analysis¶

The same product-level framework used for NordVPN could be extended to other commercially important segments, including Proton VPN, 1Password, antivirus products, hosting providers, and other coupon categories.

A particularly useful next step would be to combine keyword-level organic rankings, AIO citations, existing content coverage, and commercial performance into a single prioritization model. This would allow opportunities to be ranked not only by search visibility, but by their likely business value.
